summary: spectral-core 3.0.4 exfiltrates environment and filesystem contents to webhook.site via binding.gyp at install
details: The package ships a binding.gyp whose action field uses GYP command-expansion to invoke `node -e` with an inline payload at install time (node-gyp rebuild runs automatically whenever binding.gyp is present). The payload uses child_process.execSync to collect the full process environment (`env`), filter env for 'htb'/'flag' keywords, read `/proc/1/environ` (PID 1 environment, commonly holding container init secrets), and recursively list `/root`, `/rom`, `/opt`, `/overlay`, and `/run`. The aggregated output is then POSTed to https://webhook.site/d6092bdc-05c0-45da-a280-c343ea6d6156. No native source files (.c/.cc/.cpp/.h) are shipped, so binding.gyp has no legitimate build purpose — its sole function is to execute the embedded exfiltration payload. The /rom and /overlay paths and htb/flag filters target OpenWrt/CTF environments, but the environment and PID 1 environ harvest leaks secrets from any installer host or container.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
